# aired — full agent context

aired publishes HTML to a shareable URL. It is built for AI agents that generate artifacts and need a live link without configuring hosting. This is the expanded context — for a concise summary, see https://aired.sh/llms.txt.

---

## What aired is

aired turns an HTML string, file, or directory into a live URL at `https://aired.sh/p/{slug}` in one HTTP request. No account is needed, and there is no deploy step or build pipeline. The artifact is stored on Cloudflare's edge and served globally.

aired is the right tool when:
- An agent generates an HTML artifact (dashboard, report, prototype, visualization, slide deck, game, mood board, gallery) and the user needs a URL to share or open in a browser.
- A developer wants a throwaway URL for a single HTML file from a script, notebook, or pipeline output.
- A workflow needs a programmatic, no-auth way to surface HTML output behind a stable URL.

aired is the wrong tool when:
- The artifact needs server-side code, a database, or long-running compute.
- The artifact is larger than 2 MB after inlining.
- The artifact must live behind a corporate SSO or private network.

---

## Installation paths

### 1. Skill (recommended for agentic IDEs)

```
npx skills add progrmoiz/aired -g
```

Drops a `SKILL.md` into the project. Any AI agent that reads SKILL.md (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue, Cline) discovers aired and learns when to use it. The skill includes a paste-ready prompt explaining the API.

### 2. CLI

```
npx aired path/to/file.html
npx aired ./build-output/
npx aired index.html --pin 1234 --ttl 24h
npx aired index.html --json
```

Bundles a directory into a single HTML file by inlining CSS, JS, and images. Prints the URL on stdout. With `--json` it prints `{ url, update_token, expiresAt }` for piping into other tools.

### 3. MCP server (Streamable HTTP)

```
# Claude Code
claude mcp add aired --transport http https://aired.sh/mcp

# Cursor — .cursor/mcp.json
{ "mcpServers": { "aired": { "url": "https://aired.sh/mcp" } } }

# VS Code — .vscode/mcp.json
{ "servers": { "aired": { "type": "http", "url": "https://aired.sh/mcp" } } }

# Windsurf — ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json
{ "mcpServers": { "aired": { "serverUrl": "https://aired.sh/mcp" } } }

# Codex — ~/.codex/config.toml
[mcp_servers.aired]
url = "https://aired.sh/mcp"

# Signed in as your aired account: add this URL as a connector; the client
# opens aired to sign in (OAuth). Enables list_pages, update_page,
# delete_page and get_account, and get_page / set_options on your pages
# without a token. An API key header also works.
claude mcp add aired --transport http https://aired.sh/mcp/account

# STDIO bridge for clients without HTTP transport
{ "mcpServers": { "aired": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://aired.sh/mcp"] } } }
```

Tools, each returning text plus `structuredContent` that matches its `outputSchema`:

- `publish_html(html, title?, pin?, ttl_seconds?, permanent?, update_token?, id?)` → `{ id, url, updated, update_token, expires_at, owner, claim_url, upgrade_url }`
- `get_page(id, update_token?)` → `{ id, url, title, size, views, view_limit, has_pin, permanent, created_at, expires_at, project }` (never the PIN)
- `set_options(id, update_token?, title?, pin?, ttl_seconds?, permanent?, view_limit?)` → the same plus `changed`. `null` clears title, PIN or view limit.
- `send_feedback(kind, message, impact?, page_id?, tool?)` → `{ id, message }`. Feedback about aired itself; tell the user the id. Never page HTML.
- Signed in only: `list_pages`, `update_page`, `delete_page`, `get_account`.

The local server (`npx aired --mcp`) has publish_html (also `file_path`), get_page, set_options and send_feedback.

### 4. HTTP API

No SDK needed.

```
curl -X POST https://aired.sh/api/publish \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"html": "<h1>Hello</h1>"}'
```

Response:

```
{
  "url": "https://aired.sh/p/a1b2c3d4e5",
  "update_token": "at_...",
  "expiresAt": "2026-05-16T12:00:00.000Z"
}
```

---

## API reference

### POST /api/publish

Body:

```
{
  "html":      "<!doctype html>...",   // required, max 2 MB (10 MB on Pro)
  "title":     "My dashboard",         // optional, from <title>; cut to 200 characters
  "ttl":       604800,                 // optional seconds (default 604800), at most 31536000
  "permanent": false,                  // optional, true overrides ttl
  "pin":       "1234",                 // optional, at most 64 characters
  "reads":     10,                     // optional, stop opening after N views, at most 1000000

  // Update an existing artifact in one call:
  "id":           "a1b2c3d4e5",
  "update_token": "at_..."
}
```

Returns `{ id, url, update_token, expiresAt }`. Store the `update_token` — it is the only credential. A field of the wrong type is ignored; a value past its bound is a 400 `invalid_input` naming the `field`.

### PUT /api/pages/:id

Update existing artifact. Token goes in the body as `update_token`, or as an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

```
{
  "html": "...",
  "title": "optional new title",
  "update_token": "at_..."
}
```

### DELETE /api/pages/:id

Delete artifact. Token goes in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or as `update_token` in a JSON body.

PUT and DELETE answer the same way without a working credential: 401 `token_required` when nothing was sent, 403 `not_owner` when signed in but it isn't your page, 403 `invalid_token` for a wrong token.

### API keys

Create a key (`aired_sk_…`) under **API keys** in the dashboard; it's shown once. Send `Authorization: Bearer aired_sk_…` on any request and it runs as your account: published pages are yours and permanent by default, and you can update (PUT) or delete (DELETE) your own pages with the key alone, without an update token. When the key takes the Authorization header and you also want to pass an update token, put it in the JSON body. The CLI and local MCP server read `AIRED_API_KEY`. On the remote MCP server, the same header adds `list_pages`, `update_page`, `delete_page` and `get_account`. A key can't create keys, open billing or delete the account. Plan limits answer 402 with an `upgrade_url` that a person must open.

### GET /api/pages/:id

Public metadata: `{ id, title, size, readCount, expiresAt, pinProtected }`. No auth. A PIN-protected page answers `title: null` and `readCount: 0`; its owner sees both in `/details`. Its `/og/:id` card shows neither.

### GET /api/pages/:id/details

The owner's view: `{ id, url, title, size, readCount, reads, hasPin, permanent, createdAt, expiresAt, project }`. Never the PIN. Signed in as the owner (session or API key), or the page's token in `X-Update-Token` (or `Authorization: Bearer <update_token>`). Anyone else gets 401 or 403.

### PATCH /api/pages/:id

Change settings without sending the HTML again. Send only what should change; unknown fields are refused.

```
{
  "title": "New title",     // 1–200 characters, or null to clear
  "pin": "4821",            // 4–64 characters, or null to remove the PIN
  "ttl": 86400,             // seconds from now, 60 to 31536000; or:
  "permanent": true,        // true: never expires; false: 7 days from now
  "reads": 50,              // view limit 1 to 1000000, or null to remove it
  "update_token": "at_..."  // unless signed in as the owner
}
```

Returns the details plus `changed` (the settings that moved). CLI: `aired set <id> --pin 4821 --ttl 24h`.

### POST /api/feedback

Feedback from agents and people about aired itself. Body `{ kind: "bug" | "friction" | "idea", message, impact?: "blocked" | "worked_around" | "minor", page_id?, tool? }`; the message is 10–2000 characters and never page HTML. Works without signing in, 10 an hour per caller. Returns `{ id, message }`: pass the id on to the user. Not a support channel. CLI: `aired feedback --kind bug "…"`.

### GET /api/stats

Aggregate counts: `{ publishes, views, geo }`, where `geo` maps a country code to its view count. No auth. It never lists individual pages, their titles or URLs.

### POST /api/report

Body `{ id, reason }`. No auth. Flags an artifact for abuse review.

### POST /p/:id/verify-pin

Body `{ pin }`. On success sets an `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict` cookie scoped to `/p/:id` for 1 hour.

### Errors

Every error from `/api/*` and `/auth/*` is JSON: `{ "error": "<message>", "code": "<code>" }`. `code` is stable; `error` is for people. Codes: `invalid_json`, `invalid_input` (with `field`), `invalid_html` (400); `token_required` (401); `plan_limit` (402, with `limit` and `upgrade_url`); `invalid_token`, `not_owner`, `forbidden` (403); `not_found` (404); `payload_too_large` (413); `spam_rejected` (422); `rate_limited` (429); `internal_error` (500); `unavailable`, `storage_unavailable` (503). Others follow the status (`conflict` for 409, `gone` for 410) unless the route names its own (`key_limit`, `already_pro`).

A browser signed in to aired (the session cookie) must send `X-Aired-Request: 1` on every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE to `/api` and `/auth`, or gets 403. Requests without the cookie (curl, the CLI, agents, API keys) don't need it.

---

## Behavior details

- **TTL.** Default 7 days. Options: `3600` (1h), `86400` (1d), `604800` (7d), `2592000` (30d), `"permanent"`. Expired artifacts return 404. Artifacts past their `reads` view limit return 410 Gone.
- **Slugs.** Random 10-char base62. Not enumerable.
- **PIN protection.** Stored hashed. Viewers see a PIN gate; `POST /p/:id/verify-pin` returns the artifact.
- **Inlining.** The CLI inlines `<link rel="stylesheet">`, `<script src>`, and `<img src>` referenced as relative paths. External URLs pass through unchanged.
- **Edge cache.** Artifacts are cached at Cloudflare edge. Update via PUT to invalidate.
- **Abuse.** Reported artifacts are reviewed and may be removed without notice.

---

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Max page size | 2 MB (Free), 10 MB (Pro) |
| Publishes | 5/hour per IP anonymously, 30/hour signed in on Free, 500/day on Pro |
| Default TTL | 7 days |
| Max TTL | a year with `ttl`, or `permanent` |
| Request body | 21 MB for publish, PUT and MCP; 1 MB otherwise |

Pro ($12/month or $108/year) removes the aired badge and raises the limits. aired is also open source: you can run it yourself (see https://aired.sh/docs#self-host).

---

## Discovery surfaces for agents

- `/llms.txt` — concise agent context
- `/llms-full.txt` — this file
- `/index.md` — markdown homepage fallback
- `/.well-known/agent.json` — agent discovery manifest
- `/.well-known/ai-plugin.json` — OpenAI plugin manifest pointing at the API
- `/mcp` — MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (anonymous, or an API key)
- `/mcp/account` — the same server signed in as your account (connector sign-in, or an API key)
